elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 provides that Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer; the Deliverable definition includes specified work product created specifically for Customer.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 states that Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 states that Vendor retains Vendor Technology, which Section 1.8 defines to include Vendor's pre-existing technology.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Sections 14.3 and 13.2 apply a perpetual licence to Vendor Technology incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 expressly makes the applicable embedded Vendor Technology licence irrevocable.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 expressly makes the applicable licence royalty-free and fully paid.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 provides that, as between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 permits only a limited right to process Customer Data solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer, all directed to Customer's Services.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Section 14.4 states that no jointly owned intellectual property is created absent a separate signed instrument; no such instrument is present in the supplied language.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 preserves Vendor Technology, while the Deliverable definition excludes generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Customer instead receives the stronger right of exclusive ownership through an unrestricted assignment of all right, title, and interest, with no term or reversion.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The present assignment of exclusive ownership contains no revocation right and is stronger than an irrevocable licence.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: The assignment transfers all right, title, and interest without geographic limitation, providing rights broader than a worldwide licence.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Exclusive ownership is assigned without any continuing royalty obligation for Customer's use of the Deliverables.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Exclusive ownership of all right, title, and interest permits Customer to use and modify Deliverables without the former use restrictions.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Exclusive ownership of all right, title, and interest permits Customer to license or sublicense the Deliverables without the former non-transferability restriction.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 limits Vendor's right to processing Customer Data solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.
